heard: astronauts never staged a strike in space. In November 1973, NASA launched Skylab 4, which was the final crewed mission to America's first space station. The crew of Gerald Carr, Edward Gibson, and William Pogg were all space rookies facing an intense 84-day schedule. As crushing workloads heavily fatigued the men, an accidental radio error caused them to miss a scheduled daily briefing. That oversight resulted in a 90-minute communications gap with ground control. The media sensationalized this brief accident as a deliberate strike in orbit. A radio conference soon resolved the scheduling tensions and lightened the workload. Yet despite the rumors, real astronauts never staged a strike in space.
